questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

Over the past 20 years, there __has been__ a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is No improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The present perfect tense is a verb tense that shows an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + has/have + V3 + object. (active voice)
 
• Object + has/have + been + V3 + subject. (passive voice)
 
 
 
• ​Example:
 
 
• *​He has played some matches for the Indian Cricket team. (active voice)*
 
• *Some matches have been played by him for the Indian Cricket team. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, we need to follow the structure in the active voice form.
 
• Since the given sentence talks about the action that continues till the present time, 'has been' is the most appropriate choice of the verb form in the** underlined part.**
 
• Thus we are left with the 1st option as the only correct choice.

 

Correct Sentence__: *Over the past 20 years, there **has been** a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. You’ve probably noticed, with great disappointment, that the battery doesn’t seem to last as long as it did when it was brand new.

B. Partial charging is just fine for lithium-ion batteries and can actually have some positive benefits for cell longevity.

C. Smartphone users are forever in search of longer battery life, but unfortunately, battery capacity inevitably declines with age.

D. However, one thing you can do to prolong the life of your battery and handset is partial charging.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CADB.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them:
 
 
• Sentence C introduces us to the subject 'the quest for longer battery life'. It is the introductory sentence and will be put in the first place.
 
• Sentence A tells us about how the battery behaves after using it for a long period of time. It will be put in second place.
 
• Sentence D tells us about a method to improve battery life. It will be put in third place.
 
• The last sentence is B as it mentions the particular type i.e. lithium-ion battery.

 
 
 

Thus, the correct order is- *Smartphone users are forever in search of longer battery life, but unfortunately, battery capacity inevitably declines with age. You’ve probably noticed, with great disappointment, that the battery doesn’t seem to last as long as it did when it was brand new. However, one thing you can do to prolong the life of your battery and handset is partial charging. Partial charging is just fine for lithium-ion batteries and can actually have some positive benefits for cell longevity.*

A. So, what exactly are we eating?

B. They found that the vegetables contained very high, toxic levels of banned pesticides and the pesticide levels were more than 1000 times the permissible levels.

C. And is our food giving rise to the many health problems today?

• Sentence A asks us a very relevant question regarding our food choices. It will be put in third place.
 
• The last sentence is C as it mentions **another repercussion** of the food that we eat these days.

 
 
 

Thus, the correct order is- *A survey conducted by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India under the Union Agriculture Ministry tested random samples of vegetables in markets all over India. options.text: Ravina asked her little brother where he would like to go to play

questions.solution:

• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• The tense of direct speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the direct speech is in an interrogative form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• The reporting verb asked will remain the same.
 
• The word '**where **will follow the removal of comma and inverted commas.
 
• Change the reported speech from interrogative to assertive.
 
• Present continuous tense (are you going) in direct speech changes to past continuous in indirect speech (**he **was going).
 
• ​The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
 
• Here 'you' will be converted into 'he' as per the subject.
 
 
 
• ​​At last line up the remaining part.

 

**Following these steps, we finally get **- *Ravina asked her little brother where he was going to play.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

They are laying new telephone cables in our colony.

options.text: New telephone cables were being laid in our colony.
New telephone cables are being laid in our colony.
New telephone cables were laid in our colony.
New telephone cables will be laid in our colony.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **New telephone cables are being laid in our colony.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The structures for both the active and passive forms for present continuous tense are given below:

 
 
• Active form- Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object
 
• Passive form- Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *He is playing a Cricket match. (active voice)*
 
• *A Cricket match is being played by him. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The given sentence is an assertive one and in the **active** voice form.
 
• Follow the passive form structure for the present continuous tense given above:
 
 
• Exchange the places of the subject and object. (They - New telephone cables)
 
• Since the given subject 'cables' is a plural noun, the auxiliary verb 'are' will also be plural.
 
• Now the **verb **will be used accordingly. (being laid)
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.

 

**Following these steps, we finally get **- *New telephone cables are being laid in our colony.*
